chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Bashir ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you intend something of the good, do not delay it, for the servant fasts on a hot day intending what is with Allah, so Allah frees him from the Fire because of it, and do not consider small what you draw near to Allah with, even if it is half a date.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of hastening good deeds and not belittling small acts of worship in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the virtue of *tabarru'* (hastening) in good deeds, warning against procrastination even when the act is difficult. He illustrates that a single fast on a scorching day can serve as a means of deliverance from the Fire, while also instructing believers not to underestimate the spiritual weight of minor acts of devotion, such as giving half a date, provided they are done with sincere intention to draw near to Allah.
